newsitem.title: POLAND: MERRILL LOWERS IRENA TO "REDUCE" RATING.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL LOWERS IRENA TO "REDUCE" RATING.

text.p: Merril Lynch in London has lowered its intermediate-term rating for Polish glassmaker Irena SA to "reduce" from "netural" as the firm has signalled a transition to lower-margin sodium-glass production.
Merrill also said in its report dated October 1 it lowered its long-term recommendation to "reduce" from "accumulate".
"While the company is worth watching for signs of improvement, we believe the stock fails to offer the requisite long term relative growth prospect for an emerging market portfolio," Merrill said.
On October 1 Irena, whose full name is Huta Szkla Gospodarczego Irena SA, closed at 23.5 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse, and after its one-to-two share split on Tuesday it closed at 12.3 zlotys.

Merrill said it was lowering its 1997 earnings-per-share (eps) forecast for Irena to 2.48 zlotys from 3.54 zlotys partly because it was unconvinced of the intermediate-term growth prospects of the firm's shift towards sodium-glass production.
Merrill also said it was reducing its 1996 eps forecast for Irena to 2.02 zlotys from 2.82 zlotys after the firm's weak first half results caused by production delays and reduced export margins.
It said the former was caused by the longer-than-expected commissioning period of Irena's new crystal furnace, the latter by a stronger zloty hurting exports.
It said Irena's first-half net profit fell 44 percent to 2.74 million zlotys and sales fell three percent to 26.1 million zlotys.
